rv.q: Black has a superb operatic metal vocal. The acoustic guitar duelling and Queen/Darkness harmonies are tremendous and some of the songs sound as if they could almost have been actual venerable rock classics had they not been accosted by two ageing comedians and packed with knowingly silly lyrics about beasts, devils, farting and “the metal”.
Lawrence Boothman is a captivating performer and Liam Moffat's script is darkly funny and moving.
With direction from Gareth Nicholls, this is a surreal and funny solo play about grief

There’s just one issue – he hates dogs. As the wise words ‘ A Dog Isn’t Just for Christmas’ project themselves across the top of Kenny Miller’s set dressing (complete with washed-out rainbow flooring), the comfy life the pair have led begins to crumble around them.
